# Information Control

## Induced ignorance as policy

> status: ratified (D-0016)

The elite's cheapest weapon is not soldiers: it is misinformation, and the engineered
ignorance of history, deployed as population control. A population that cannot reason
about the past cannot audit the present. This thread runs through everything — it is
why the ledger of *this repo* exists in the world's own image.

## Linguistic enclosure

> status: provisional (D-0072)

The working model: the empire fences language the way it fences pasture. Words for
shared ownership, reciprocity, and balance are outlawed, taxed out of common speech,
or redefined into servility — because a spoken-proof world makes vocabulary into
capability. If you lack the words for "the valley holds this river in common," you
cannot speak the proof that makes it true again.

## Weaponized folklore

> status: provisional (D-0072)

The empire manufactures explanations. State-seeded tales blame the land's sickness on
the poor's own failings — insufficient tithes, impiety, laziness — so that villages
police themselves and each other. (The modern mirror — blame-shifting propaganda,
"your footprint" — stays in the authors' room per D-0030.) Some of the oppressed
believe it fervently; penitent movements that scourge their own communities for the
weather are among the world's saddest sights.

## Geasa as gag orders

> status: provisional (D-0072)

Drawn from the Irish geas: binding spoken obligations. The empire's scribes bind
village headmen and licensed tradesfolk with formal geasa whose breach rebounds
physically — an internalized censorship that needs no informer. Untying someone's geas
without destroying them is delicate, dangerous work, and one of the protagonist's most
subversive services.

## The false curriculum

> status: provisional (D-0072)

Where the empire does teach, it teaches a closed loop: a sanctioned, deliberately
crippled logic that always resolves in the ledger's favor, whose predictable failures
convince the taught that truth itself belongs to their betters. Against this, the act
of real teaching — a child shown how to actually reason — is sedition
([[apprentice]], D-0021).

## The keep-stamped deck
> status: ratified (D-0148)

The false curriculum has an object: the keep-stamped oracular deck ([[the-turning]]). The empire
cannot ban the leaves, so it licenses them — clean, respectable decks whose hardest Weathers, the
Debt and the Sundering and the Bourn, have been cut out, so a frightened reader can never reach
the question of who owes what to whom. It is a tool for the mind, sold as a kindness and built to
keep a mind from its own thinking — the deck-scale twin of the crippled logic above. Played
straight, the rig is never named aloud ([[economy]]).

## Memory policing

> status: provisional (D-0072)

The long institutional war on remembering: standing stones broken
([[breaking-of-the-stones]]), skalds drowned or scattered, the young drafted away from
their elders before transmission can finish ([[tithe-of-minds-sweeps]]), the bound
book replacing the living reciter. What survived, survived in hems and lullabies and
bog-sunk bundles — carried disproportionately by women, which is precisely why the
empire calls it witchery ([[womens-lives]]).
